The derivative hypothesis is checked in Lean for arbitrary F. For the second, start with the nondegenerate Bernoulli law (delta0+delta1)/2 and contaminate by mass t^2 at 1/2+1/t^2. Each law has finite second moment, the CDF perturbation divided by t tends uniformly to zero, and the mean changes by one, contradicting every continuous linear derivative. All suprema and integrals used in the refutation are legitimate; see nonvacuity.md.

This correctly refutes the printed fixed-x reading. Let X be fair binary, with Y conditionally Bernoulli of success probability 1/4 at X=0 and 3/4 at X=1. Fit the covariate-independent Bernoulli family t in [1/4,3/4]. The fixed covariate x=0 has probability 1/2 and unique conditional-KL minimizer 1/4, while the measurable actual-product MLE, the clipped success fraction, tends to 1/2. Normalizations, support domination and finite KL integrands hold, and the maximizer exists on every sample. This is not a refutation of the alternative expected-KL target; see nonvacuity.md.

This correctly refutes full-vector consistency and hence the printed conjunction. Take b0=3/4, p=1 and a=1/3, giving the IID law (2/3,1/3,0,0). A count-based product maximizer, defined on every sample, can choose b_hat=1/4 whenever no inactive-component outcome occurs. This occurs almost surely under the true law, leaving the estimated b coordinate a fixed distance 1/2 from b0. Both component parameter domains are nonempty; the failure is genuine nonidentifiability, not an empty optimizer condition. See nonvacuity.md for the full estimator.

This correctly refutes the stated asymptotic size bound. Let X be uniform on {-1,0,1}, Z a fair sign independent of X, D conditionally Bernoulli(1/4+X^2/2) independent of Z given X, and W=X^2+Z/2. The twelve cell probabilities are 1/8 or 1/24. W and D are conditionally independent given X. Lean checks cell normalization, restricted/full Gram determinants 2/3 and 17/54, full coefficient (29/68,0,4/17), and positive full risk 59/272. The restricted risk is 35/144, so F_n/n tends almost surely to 64/531>0. Both regressions are eventually nonsingular, actual F(1,n-3) medians stay bounded, and guarded rejection probability tends to one. See scratch/Check.lean and nonvacuity.md.

Use IID standard Gaussians with their continuous PDF and h_n=1/sqrt(n+1). Bandwidths are positive, tend to zero and satisfy n h_n tending to infinity. The kernel is bounded at each bandwidth; its expectation is the local density average and its variance is at most that average divided by 2 n h_n. No nonintegrable expectation or zero bandwidth is used. This is the pointwise consistency claim read with its printed continuous-density condition.

For standard normal Z take theta_hat_n=theta+phi Z/sqrt(n+1) and v_hat_n=phi^2/(n+1), with phi>0 and any 0<alpha<1. In general Slutsky and continuity at both Gaussian boundaries give the stated coverage limit, without a limsup convention or a coverage hypothesis.

Take IID fair Bernoulli outcomes, constant X, reference delta0+delta1, parameter interval [1/4,3/4] and the usual Bernoulli family with true parameter 1/2. The clipped sample success fraction is an actual-product maximizer. M(t)=(log t+log(1-t))/2 is continuous with unique maximum 1/2; all observed logs are finite and observed model densities positive. For n>0, Delta_n=log(3)|sample success fraction-1/2| uniformly bounds every log-likelihood error, and Delta_0=2 handles the initial sample. The WLLN gives Delta_n tending to zero. Thus the envelope premise is nonvacuous and does not assume estimator convergence. The independently quantified maximum/equality lemma has the same true normalized model as an instance. The record and docstring accurately disclose the uniform premise, its pointwise quantifiers and the omitted auxiliary conclusions; see nonvacuity.md.
